newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares edge to new heights, H&M jumps.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares edge to new heights, H&M jumps.

text.p: 1525 - Swedish share prices inched to a fresh record on Monday, bolstered by gains in telecoms group Ericsson and clothing retailer Hennes & Maurtiz which hit a high after better-than-expected first half results.
* Stockholm bourse general index rises 0.14 percent to 2,919.38 in turnover totalling 3.8 billion crowns

* Ericsson up 2.5 crowns to 302 after a positive analysis * H&M leaps 26 crowns to an all-time intra-day high of 293 but closed at 285.5, up 18.5 crowns after the company says pre-tax profit surged 63 percent to 1.01 billion crowns in the first half of its 1996/1997 fiscal year
Share prices inched to a fresh record on Monday, bolstered by gains in telecoms group Ericsson and Hennes & Mauritz.
The bourse general index rose 0.14 percent to 2,919.38 in turnover totalling 3.8 billion crowns.

Clothing retailer H&M leapt 26 crowns to an all-time intra-day high of 293 but closed at 285.5, up 18.5 crowns after the company said pre-tax profit surged 63 percent to 1.01 billion crowns in the first half of its 1996/1997 fiscal year.
Analysts in a Reuter poll targeted 832 million crowns.
Analysts said the group's operating margins were impressive but several said the share was expensive.
Ericsson rose 2.5 crowns to 302 after a positive analysis from investment bank Merrill Lynch, brokers said.
The session's most traded share was vehicle maker AB Volvo, which fell 3.5 crowns to 203 in turnover of 532 million crowns.
Morgan Grenfell Asset Management Ltd said it sold its entire stake in Swedish casting equipment group SinterCast, which fell 33 crowns to 109.
